subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What memory lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for review, edit, forget, tombstone/supersede, and conflict resolution across memory plugins?
rationale: The gap is real, but the correct solution depends on durable storage, privacy, audit, rollback, plugin API, and operator UX choices that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Define lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle the memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface work.

options.title: Limit v1 to memory-core
options.body: Implement only the bundled memory-core CLI and SQLite behavior now, accepting that external memory plugins will need later API alignment.

options.title: Defer lifecycle MVP
options.body: Leave current search, promotion, and dreaming behavior in place and track concrete stale-memory bugs separately until memory lifecycle becomes a priority.

recommendation.title: Define lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle the memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface work.

likelyOwner.reason: The requested lifecycle contract depends most directly on current memory storage/schema and SDK event-journal ownership history.
